intro: QI Connector is a remote MCP server that exposes the QI ecosystem to Claude as a set of callable tools. It holds no data of its own — every tool is a thin, bounded proxy onto the Brain API or the registry, which is what keeps the public surface small and auditable.

snippets.title: Self-provisioning bearer + path tokens
snippets.code:
def _load_or_create_token(fname: str) -> str:
    f = ROOT / "secrets" / fname
    f.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    if f.exists():
        return f.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip()
    tok = pysecrets.token_urlsafe(32)
    f.write_text(tok, encoding="utf-8")
    log.info("generated new token file %s", fname)
    return tok


BEARER_TOKEN = _load_or_create_token("connector_token.txt")
PATH_TOKEN = _load_or_create_token("connector_path_token.txt")
snippets.explanation: Both tokens are generated once with secrets.token_urlsafe(32) and persisted under secrets/, so a fresh deployment secures itself with no manual key ceremony and no secret in source control. The path token is embedded in the connector URL, which makes that URL itself a credential — it must be treated as a password and rotated by deleting the token file and restarting.

snippets.title: Single bounded call into the Brain API
snippets.feature: Every tool is a thin proxy
snippets.explanation: All Brain-backed tools funnel through this one helper: a short-timeout httpx POST that raises on any non-2xx. Centralising it means timeout and error behaviour are uniform across the whole tool surface rather than reimplemented per tool.

snippets.title: Response clipping
snippets.feature: Bounded payloads back to the model
snippets.explanation: Tool results are clipped before being returned. An unbounded Brain response would otherwise flow straight into the model's context window and could blow it out in a single call.
